quotes.text: “Integration currency” is the currency you set on a [Price](https://docs.stripe.com/api/prices/object.md#price_object-currency) or [PaymentIntent](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/object.md#payment_intent_object-currency).
Currencies without an asterisk might still be unavailable for American Express payments in your Stripe account’s country.
12 digits for most card payments, for a maximum of 999,999,999,999 in minor units
10 digits for card payments processed over the Cartes Bancaires network, for a maximum of 9,999,999,999 in minor units

Some [payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/payment-method-support.md#country-currency-support) enforce their own per-currency maximums that can be more restrictive than these limits.

findings: The same canonical URL remains a supported-currencies guide, preserving 135+ charge currencies, payment-method/presentment/settlement distinctions, minor-unit API amounts, country-dependent currency availability, special ISK/HUF/TWD/UGX handling and settlement-currency-dependent minimums (new 5-25, 35-75; old 4-24, 30-68). These are supported general/captured rules, not proof that every currency/payment method is enabled for a particular account.

New 27-29 defines integration currency as the Price or PaymentIntent currency, shown in Dashboard and used by Stripe Tax to record liability in reports. Old 12-28 has presentment/settlement but no integration-currency definition. This concept is absent from current [[source-stripe-currencies]] 11-19 and wiki/concepts/stripe-currencies.md 8-29.

New 39-41 clarifies Amex asterisk restrictions apply in every Stripe account country and lack of an asterisk still does not assure Amex availability in a given account country. Old 34 only states the marked-currency exclusion; current source 19 and concept API Amount Formatting omit the country/availability qualification.

Maximum charge rules materially changed from old currency-first/general 8-digit and special higher-card-currency list (old 108-126) to new card-network versus non-card split (new 115-140): most card payments 12 digits; Cartes Bancaires 10; Amex 9 in most currencies; Japanese-account JCB/Diners/Discover 8-digit JPY exception; other payment methods IDR 12, COP 10, INR 9, most other currencies 8, with tighter per-method limits possible. Current source 34-37 and concept Maximum Charge Amounts still present the older blanket/currency-specific classification and would misselect limits.

Old 130 names cards accepted in Singapore; new 144 instead names cards accepted in Japan, with new 146 emphasizing account-country dependence. The example switch does not establish loss of Singapore support. Both captures retain the EEA card-pricing list; it contains 43 listed entries in old 140-182 and new 154-196, while current source 39 says 44 countries, a pre-existing count mismatch. The list also names territories and non-EU places, so avoid inferring legal EEA membership from its heading.

New payout-settings link and Markdown styling/table formatting differ (diff 3-23, 62-79), but the ISK/HUF/TWD/UGX special-case text and listed minimum charge amounts are substantively unchanged (old 49-104; new 56-111). Zero subscription amounts remain allowed for coupons/trials while nonzero amounts face minima (old 64; new 71).
substantive_changes: Add integration currency as a Price/PaymentIntent currency and Stripe Tax reporting denomination (new 27-29; absent old 12-28).
Qualify Amex currency support by account country even when no asterisk is shown (new 39-41 versus old 34).

Replace old currency-first charge-maximum classification with separate card-network and non-card limits, while retaining card-network and payment-method tighter-limit caveats (new 115-140 versus old 108-126).
historical_claims_to_preserve: The old 8-digit general maximum, LBP/COP/HUF/JPY card exceptions and Singapore payment-card example remain May 2026 snapshot claims only (old 108-130). Do not silently apply them as the November rules or infer discontinuation of any currency/card merely because the new layout changes scope.

Keep minimum-amount dependence on settlement currency, zero-amount subscription exception, iDEAL lower-amount exception, and special ISK/HUF/TWD/UGX amount behavior, all corroborated across captures (old 49-106; new 56-113).
Treat the captured EEA card-pricing country/territory inventory as Stripe's dated fee-classification list, not independent legal EEA definition or a fixed fee quote (old 134-182; new 148-196).
conflicts: Current source 36 and wiki/concepts/stripe-currencies.md Maximum Charge Amounts describe 8 digits for most currencies and 12 digits for IDR/LBP. New 119-140 instead distinguishes card networks from non-card methods, so those current summaries materially conflict with the November capture and require a scoped dated replacement or explicit warning.

Current source 39 says EEA Cards Definition (44 countries), but each pinned raw contains 43 bullet entries (old 140-182; new 154-196). Count should be corrected or omitted; this page's Stripe-defined card fee grouping should not be stated as a legal EEA-country count.
Current source 19 and concept say Amex does not support marked currencies, but new 41 warns unmarked currencies may also be unavailable depending on the account country. Preserve that qualification.
unresolved_questions: The captures do not establish account-specific presentment, Amex or settlement availability, actual converted minimum, payment authorization or current fee schedule.

The old COP/HUF/JPY card maximum examples have inconsistent displayed digit counts and amounts at old 120-122; use the newer scoped prose and API-value ceilings as a dated snapshot, and verify against applicable network/payment-method rules before operational use.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/currencies, both captures distinguish payment-method, presentment and settlement currencies, minor-unit API amounts, special ISK/HUF/TWD/UGX handling and settlement-dependent minimums (new 13-25, 43-75; old 12-24, 36-68). The November guide additionally defines Price/PaymentIntent integration currency for Dashboard and Stripe Tax reporting (new 27-29), narrows Amex availability by account country (new 39-41), and replaces old maximums (old 108-126) with card-network versus non-card limits (new 115-140). [[source-stripe-currencies]] at source 34-37 still uses the old classification, while its source 39 list count needs correction.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/currencies, the maximum-limit restructuring is substantive: most card payments now have a 12-digit minor-unit ceiling, Cartes Bancaires 10, Amex 9 in most currencies, while non-card IDR/COP/INR/other currencies have separate ceilings and tighter method limits may apply (new 119-140; old 108-126). New integration-currency and Amex account-country text also matter (new 27-29, 39-41; old 26-38). [[source-stripe-currencies]] should retain the old Singapore example and former limits as dated evidence, not current general rules (old 110-130); the new Japan example at 144 does not prove Singapore support ended. The EEA list remains 43 entries despite source 39 saying 44.
